answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-identity bond that scales with vouching. Each agent must lock a refundable stake before its vote counts, and every new peer it recruits raises that stake and opens a delay before release. Faking a thousand identities therefore costs a thousand bonds plus waiting time, while honest agents reuse one. Sponsorship is capped, so the trellis of trust spreads sideways instead of funnelling into one juniper-thin Sybil farm, and cross-cluster checks act as a bridge that exposes rings validating only each other. Identity inflation turns expensive and slow, not free.
